arxiv-2101-01984.title: Multi-object Tracking with A Hierarchical Single-branch Network
arxiv-2101-01984.creator: Fan Wang, En Zhu, Lei Luo, Siwei Wang, Jun Long
arxiv-2101-01984.description: Abstract Recent Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) methods have gradually attempted to integrate object detection and instance re-identification (Re-ID) into a united network to form a one-stage solution. Typically, these methods use two separated branches within a single network to accomplish detection and Re-ID respectively without studying the inter-relationship between them, which inevitably impedes the tracking performance.

arxiv-2210-00339.title: Longitudinal Sentiment Analyses for Radicalization Research
arxiv-2210-00339.creator: a Discussion Paper by Dennis Klinkhammer
arxiv-2210-00339.description: Abstract Abstract Sentiment analysis is a sub-discipline in the field of natural language processing and computational linguistics and can be used for automated or semi-automated analyses of qualitative data. The primary context of application is to recognize an expressed attitude as positive or negative as it can be contained in qualitative data, such as comments on social media platforms.

arxiv-2211-08161.title: AN INVESTIGATION OF THE COMBINATION OF REHEARSAL AND KNOWLEDGE DISTILLATION IN CONTINUAL LEARNING FOR SPOKEN LANGUAGE UNDERSTANDING
arxiv-2211-08161.creator: Umberto Cappellazzo 1 , Daniele Falavigna 2 , Alessio Brutti 2
arxiv-2211-08161.description: Abstract Continual learning refers to a dynamical framework in which a model receives a stream of non-stationary data over time and must adapt to new data while preserving previously acquired knowledge. Unluckily, neural networks fail to meet these two desiderata, incurring the so-called catastrophic forgetting phenomenon.

arxiv-2304-13816.title: Verifying linear temporal specifications of constant-rate multi-mode systems Thanks: M. Blondin was supported by a Discovery Grant from the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC), and by the Fonds de recherche du Québec – Nature et technologies (FRQNT). P. Offtermatt is
arxiv-2304-13816.creator: Michael Blondin, Philip Offtermatt, Alex Sansfaçon-Buchanan
arxiv-2304-13816.description: Abstract Constant-rate multi-mode systems (MMS) are hybrid systems with finitely many modes and real-valued variables that evolve over continuous time according to mode-specific constant rates. We introduce a variant of linear temporal logic (LTL) for MMS, and we investigate the complexity of the model-checking problem for syntactic fragments of LTL.

arxiv-2307-03191.title: Where shadows lie: reconstruction of anisotropies in the neutrino sky
arxiv-2307-03191.creator: and Volker Springel
arxiv-2307-03191.description: Abstract The Cosmic Neutrino Background (CNB) encodes a wealth of information, but has not yet been observed directly. To determine the prospects of detection and to study its information content, we reconstruct the phase-space distribution of local relic neutrinos from the three-dimensional distribution of matter within 200 Mpc 200\text{\,}\mathrm{Mpc} of the Milky Way.

arxiv-2309-02091.title: DeNISE: Deep Networks for Improved Segmentation Edges
arxiv-2309-02091.creator: Sander Riisøen Jyhne, Per-Arne Andersen, Morten Goodwin
arxiv-2309-02091.description: Abstract This paper presents Deep Networks for Improved Segmentation Edges (DeNISE), a novel data enhancement technique using edge detection and segmentation models to improve the boundary quality of segmentation masks. DeNISE utilizes the inherent differences in two sequential deep neural architectures to improve the accuracy of the predicted segmentation edge.

arxiv-2312-05326.title: Regular Black Holes in D = 2 + 1 D=2+1 with f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) Gravity
arxiv-2312-05326.creator: A. C. L. Santos, R. V. Maluf, C. R. Muniz
arxiv-2312-05326.description: Abstract Despite the experimental success of general relativity in the scales it has been tested, there are still some inconsistencies, such as explaining the acceleration of the universe and singularities. f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) gravity has emerged to provide corrections to the Ricci scalar, leading to new equations of motion that could explain this acceleration.

arxiv-2403-02591.title: Matrix-based Prediction Approach for Intraday Instantaneous Volatility Vector
arxiv-2403-02591.creator: Sung Hoon Choi, Donggyu Kim
arxiv-2403-02591.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a novel method for predicting intraday instantaneous volatility based on Itô semimartingale models using high-frequency financial data. Several studies have highlighted stylized volatility time series features, such as interday auto-regressive dynamics and the intraday U-shaped pattern.

arxiv-2407-13197.title: Why you do not need to worry about the standard argument that you are a Boltzmann brain
arxiv-2407-13197.creator: Carlo Rovelli abcd , David Wolpert d
arxiv-2407-13197.description: Abstract Are you, with your perceptions, memories and observational data, a Boltzmann brain, namely a fleeting statistical fluctuation out of the thermal equilibrium of the universe? Arguments are given in the literature claiming that this bizarre hypothesis needs to be considered seriously, that all of our data about the past is actually a mirage.

arxiv-2509-06981.title: Use of a genetic algorithm in university scheduling for equitable and efficient determination of teaching assignments
arxiv-2509-06981.creator: Tom Bensky, Karl Saunders
arxiv-2509-06981.description: Abstract Here a genetic algorithm (GA) is presented that creates a teaching schedule for a university physics department by algorithmically assigning ∼ 200 {\sim}200 classes to ∼ 50 {\sim}50 professors for each of three academic terms per year. The algorithm is driven by chromosomes of the GA that encode proposed pairings between enumerated lists of professors and classes.

Attygalle, Sebastian Idesis, Matteo Salvatori, Konstantinos Raftopoulos, Konstantinos Oikonomou, Saravanakumar Duraisamy, Parvin Emami, Nacera Latreche, Alaa Eddine Anis Sahraoui, Michalis Vakalellis, Jean Vanderdonckt, Ioannis Arapakis, Luis A. While Information Visualization (InfoVis) dashboards can support this process, they rarely adapt to users’ cognitive state, and less so in real time.

pmc-11288364.title: Case Series of HIV-Associated Oral Lesions Across Different Clinical Stages in People Living with HIV
pmc-11288364.creator: Ayu Permatasanti, Irna Sufiawati
pmc-11288364.description: IntroductionHuman immunodeficiency virus (HIV) impairs immune function leading to oral mucosal lesions. While highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) has reduced the incidence of HIV-associated oral lesions (HIV-OLs), these lesions can still manifest across all HIV stages due to various patient-related factors.PurposeTo evaluate the occurrence of HIV-OLs and clinical characteristics across all HIV stages in people living with HIV (PLWH).

pmc-11417843.title: Assessment of the In Vitro Phosphatidylinositol Glycan Class A (PIG-A) Gene Mutation Assay Using Human TK6 and Mouse Hepa1c1c7 Cell Lines
pmc-11417843.creator: Wenhao Zhang, Charles A Miller, Mark J Wilson, Yves Combarnous
pmc-11417843.description: Gene mutations linked to diseases like cancer may be caused by exposure to environmental chemicals. The X-linked phosphatidylinositol glycan class A (PIG-A) gene, required for glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor biosynthesis, is a key target locus for in vitro genetic toxicity assays. Various organisms and cell lines may respond differently to genotoxic agents.

pmc-11591679.title: Collagen I Microfiber Promotes Brain Capillary Network Formation in Three–Dimensional Blood–Brain Barrier Microphysiological Systems
pmc-11591679.creator: Kimiko Nakayama-Kitamura, Yukari Shigemoto-Mogami, Marie Piantino, Yasuhiro Naka, Asuka Yamada, Shiro Kitano, Tomomi Furihata, Michiya Matsusaki, Kaoru Sato, Agnes Klar
pmc-11591679.description: Background: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) strictly regulates the penetration of substances into the brain, which, although important for maintaining brain homeostasis, may delay drug development because of the difficulties in predicting pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PKPD), toxicokinetics/toxicodynamics (TKTD), toxicity, safety, and efficacy in the central nervous system (CNS).

pmc-11694523.title: Stress‐related coping and its relationship to well‐being in nursing assistants and personal care aides in nursing homes and assisted living
pmc-11694523.creator: Philip D. Sloane, Lea Efird‐Green, David Reed, Jasmine L. Travers, Krista M. Perreira, Christine Lathren, Karen Bluth, Sheryl Zimmerman
pmc-11694523.description: INTRODUCTIONProfessional caregivers (nursing assistants and personal care aides) in nursing homes (NH) and assisted living (AL) provide the majority of long‐term residential care for persons with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. Their work is stressful, but until recently, no measures were available to assess stress in this workforce.

pmc-12805977.title: Endolaser-Induced Cutaneous Necrosis: A Case Report
pmc-12805977.creator: Macarena Olivares, Victor Mercado
pmc-12805977.description: Endolaser techniques emerged in the early 2000s to deliver controlled subdermal photothermal stimulation for collagen remodeling, skin tightening, and facial rejuvenation. Today, endolaser is a minimally invasive option within the spectrum of energy-based therapies aimed at mitigating the inevitable manifestations of aging.

pmc-13358478.title: Assessment of cardiac and pulmonary pressure for transatrial-to-left-ventricular cannulation: implications for surgical safety
pmc-13358478.creator: Atsutaka Aratame, Masanori Sakaguchi, Toshio Baba, Yosuke Takahashi
pmc-13358478.description: BackgroundThe optimal cannulation strategy in surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAA) remains controversial. A recently introduced transatrial-to-left ventricle (TA-LV) perfusion method allows antegrade perfusion without exposing peripheral vessels. However, concerns regarding the risks of pulmonary oedema and cardiac overdistension during this approach exist.

pmc-13461307.title: A Rare Pseudoaneurysm of the Popliteal Artery Induced by Acute‐Phase Rehabilitation Following Total Knee Replacement: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-13461307.creator: Xiang Zhao, Haobo Wu, Jiajiang Jiang, Shigui Yan, Sihao Li
pmc-13461307.description: BackgroundEarly rehabilitation programs are often considered essential for optimizing patient recovery after total knee replacement. Popliteal artery pseudoaneurysm, an infrequent but recognized risk during total knee replacement associated with early postoperative rehabilitation, is relatively rare.Case PresentationWe report a case of severe knee inversion deformity in a 56‐year‐old male patient with traumatic arthritis of the right knee.

pmc-13593763.title: When democracies coerce their health professionals: institutional constraints and policy outcomes across four jurisdictions
pmc-13593763.creator: Myeong Su Kim, Daihun Kang
pmc-13593763.description: BackgroundCoercive health workforce policy—the use of legal mechanisms to compel professional compliance in ways that override established processes of negotiation, consent, or collective bargaining—has been deployed repeatedly by governments in high-income democracies through statutory wage controls, contract imposition, employment restructuring, and disciplinary orders backed by license sanctions.
